task.description: Hard gate on Step 2a: moduledoc text replacement in lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex, plus 5 new e2e tests (test/letflow/router_test.exs, test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs). Verify against INV-1..INV-8.

result.summary:
Scope check: `git diff main...HEAD --stat` shows only expected files -- both plug moduledocs, the two test files, the design doc, and this run's own handoffs/status bookkeeping. No lib code logic changed (confirmed via `git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex`: only the docstring paragraph differs, `@behaviour`/`call/2`/`check_write_pause/2` untouched). This is a tenant-data path per the handoff brief (AuthPipeline resolves tenant identity + JIT-provisions users; TenantStatus does a fail-closed Repo.get(Tenant, tenant_id)), so the scope test result is: IN SCOPE, invariants assessed below.

INV-1 (tenant isolation): APPLIES (diff touches tests that exercise tenant-scoped plug behavior, though no schema/migration changed this run). Verified: no new Ecto schema/migration in this diff -- (a)/(b)/(c) of the verification procedure are moot since no business-table schema or migration was added or changed. The new test helper `insert_tenant_for_realm!/1` in api_pipeline_integration_test.exs generates a fresh tenant per test via `unique_slug/1` (System.unique_integer, monotonic+positive) rather than reusing a fixed tenant_id across cases, and cleans up its own tenant row + schema in `on_exit/1` -- no cross-test tenant_id leakage or hardcoded reuse found. PASS.

INV-2, INV-3, INV-5: NOT APPLICABLE. No response-shaping/field-selection code touched (no new API response type); no scripting/sandbox code touched; no new lookup-by-ID endpoint added (TenantStatus's existing Repo.get(Tenant, tenant_id) call is pre-existing logic, unchanged this run).

INV-4 (secrets by reference only): APPLIES (checkable now). `grep -rn "System.get_env" config/ lib/` shows only env-sourced config (DATABASE_URL, PORT, POOL_SIZE, LETFLOW_DB_PORT, test-partition vars) -- no hardcoded secret literals. Heuristic hardcoded-secret grep against lib/ and config/ (excluding test/) returned no hits needing manual override. This run's own moduledoc text and test code introduce no new secret material (test bearer token `"valid-test-token"` is an established test-double convention, not a real credential -- consistent with existing auth_pipeline_test.exs precedent). PASS.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove scoping): this handoff itself is the mechanism -- satisfied by this document existing with status PASS and this explicit per-invariant accounting.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation): APPLIES. `grep -rn "Repo.query" lib/ priv/repo/migrations/` shows raw-SQL hits only in pre-existing files (tenant_provisioning.ex, sandbox_pool.ex, fixture_loader.ex) unrelated to this diff -- confirmed none of those lines changed in `git diff main...HEAD`. The new test file api_pipeline_integration_test.exs contains one `Repo.query!(~s(DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS "#{schema_name}" CASCADE))` in its cleanup helper: schema_name is server-derived (via TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1, not caller/tenant-controlled free text) and this exact pattern is an established precedent already used identically in test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs and in production code (tenant_provisioning.ex:188, sandbox_pool.ex:298/321) for CREATE/DROP SCHEMA statements, which cannot be parameterised via Ecto's query API (identifiers, not values). Not a new risk introduced by this run. PASS.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): APPLIES, and is the load-bearing property this run's Test 5 (AC5) exists to prove. Read test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs lines 186-218 directly: two `Task.async/1` calls are started before either is awaited (genuine BEAM-level concurrency, not sequential simulation), both running in Sandbox `:auto` mode (real pool connections, real committed Postgres state per the module's own async:false rationale, not a shared per-test transaction). The bad task calls `TenantStatus.call/2` with a malformed tenant_id ("not-a-uuid"), rescues in its own process, and asserts it crashes with `Ecto.Query.CastError` (confirming TenantStatus's deliberate no-rescue fail-closed design, per tenant_status.ex's own moduledoc and check_write_pause/2 body -- no try/rescue was added, matching Step 2a's explicit constraint). The good task concurrently resolves a real, valid tenant and completes with `refute good_conn.halted` / `status == nil` (unhalted, pass-through). This soundly demonstrates that one request's crash does not affect a concurrently in-flight request for a different tenant -- satisfying the OTP-per-request-process isolation this invariant requires. Also spot-checked `grep -rn "^\s*{:ok, .*} = " lib/letflow/` for new bare-match crashes: no hits inside this diff's changed lib files (auth_pipeline.ex, tenant_status.ex had no logic changes at all). PASS.

No issues filed -- nothing adjacent or out-of-scope found worth queuing.
